name: Contact Lenses
description: TSA rules for flying with contact lenses, blister packs, lens cases, and contact solution in carry-on and checked luggage.

carryOn.reason: Contact lenses in sealed blister packs and contact lens cases are fully allowed in carry-on baggage. Contact lens solution is classified as a medically necessary liquid and is exempt from the standard 3.4 oz liquids rule.
conditions: Contact lens blister packs containing saline solution are permitted in carry-on bags without counting against your 3-1-1 liquids limit.
Large bottles of contact lens solution (> 3.4 oz / 100ml) are medically exempt, but must be declared to the TSA officer at the checkpoint for separate screening.

checkedBag.reason: Contact lenses, extra cases, and bottles of lens solution are fully allowed in checked baggage with no restrictions.
conditions: Keep valuable specialty lenses in your carry-on to avoid loss if checked bags are delayed.

tsa.pageTitle: Can I bring contact lenses on a plane?

airlines.name: Delta Air Lines
airlines.notes: Contact lenses and eye care products permitted in cabin and checked luggage.

airlines.name: Emirates
airlines.notes: Contact lenses and medically necessary eye solutions allowed in hand baggage.

travelTips: Always pack several extra pairs of daily contact lenses and your eyeglasses in your carry-on in case of travel delays or dry cabin air.
Airplane cabin air is notoriously dry — bring travel-size rewetting drops (under 3.4 oz) or switch to glasses during long-haul flights.
Declare any large bottles of contact lens solution to the TSA agent before bag screening starts.

faq.question: Do contact lens blister packs count as liquids under TSA 3-1-1?
faq.answer: TSA treats sealed contact lens blister packs as personal medical supplies. While they contain a small amount of saline, TSA generally allows them in your carry-on without requiring you to fit them into your quart-sized liquids bag.

faq.question: Can I bring a full-size bottle of contact solution in my carry-on?
faq.answer: Yes! Contact lens solution is officially classified by the TSA as an over-the-counter medically necessary liquid. You are allowed to bring bottles larger than 3.4 oz (100ml) in your carry-on, but you must remove the bottle and declare it to the officer for separate inspection.

faq.question: Can I wear contact lenses during a flight?
faq.answer: Yes, but aircraft cabins have low humidity (often under 20%), which can cause severe dry eyes and lens discomfort. It is recommended to bring lubricating eye drops or wear glasses during flights over 4 hours.
